title: Investigate aggregation anomaly in embedding usage for enterprise account causing unexpected overage
creator: Miguel Santos
description:
Summary: Enterprise customer 'Atlas Analytics' reported a 3x jump in embedding usage on 2026-03-06 resulting in a large overage charge. Customer asserts they did not change traffic patterns. Support escalated; customer requests immediate credit and root-cause explanation.

Observed behavior: Billing export shows a spike in 'embedding_units' attributed to model 'embed-large-v2' between 2026-03-05 23:30 UTC and 2026-03-06 03:45 UTC. The spike is concentrated in aggregated daily buckets on the billing job output (billing_daily_aggregates table). Raw request logs (serving logs) do not show a proportional increase in successful token/embedding calls; instead we observed a surge in meter events during intermediate aggregation runs.

Initial hypothesis: A race condition in the hourly->daily aggregation pipeline duplicated aggregation rows when the hourly job retried after a transient BigQuery write timeout. Two paths create meter events: (1) the serving-side metering emitter and (2) the aggregation job that imports hourly counters and writes daily aggregates. Retry behavior in the aggregation job lacked idempotency guarding for the same time-window/key which allowed double-counting. Additional contributors: clock skew between aggregator instances and the billing job leading to overlapping windows, and a late-arriving 'preflight' meter envelope from the gateway that was treated as a distinct event instead of being merged.

Impact: Customer billed ~USD 62k over expected for the billing period. Customer usage patterns flagged as high customer_impact; immediate remediation and credits required. We estimate 1 customer directly affected (Atlas Analytics) but runbook checks requested to scan other enterprise customers for similar duplicates.
comments: 2026-03-08 09:12 - Support (Emily Zhao): Received escalation from Atlas PM. Attached billing CSV and customer's traffic chart. Customer requests provisional $40k credit while investigation ongoing. Ticket raised to ENG.

2026-03-08 11:45 - Triage (Miguel Santos): Reproduced discrepancy between billing_daily_aggregates and raw_events for the same time window. Created billing query to surface duplicate aggregate rows: https://bigquery.redwood.example/project/datasets/billing/queries/AGG_DUP_FIND. Added to ENG backlog.

2026-03-09 15:30 - Investigation (Aisha Patel): Ran full-scan across last 90 days for duplicate (customer_id, model, date) aggregates where sum(hourly_hash) != aggregate_value. Found 7 abnormal buckets across 2 customers (Atlas + internal dev org). Preliminary root-cause points to aggregator job retried after transient INSERT failure; INSERT mode used 'append' without dedupe key.

2026-03-10 10:02 - Mitigation (Aisha Patel): Deployed hotfix to aggregation job: switch BigQuery write mode to 'upsert' using dedupe key (customer_id, model, window_start). Added short-term webhook to mark suspect aggregates and flag billing pipeline to avoid finalizing invoices for flagged windows. Patch PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/billing/pull/2781

2026-03-11 16:20 - Validation (Data Eng - Rajiv Kumar): Backfilled corrected aggregates for affected windows and re-run invoice simulation. Atlas overage reduced from $62k to $4.2k. Generated repro playbook for future detection. Dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/billing/duplicate-aggregates

2026-03-12 09:00 - Customer communication (Support - Emily Zhao): Notified Atlas that we identified the root cause and have provisional credit plan. Requested acceptance to apply credit once accounting verifies. Customer accepted provisional resolution and requested a postmortem.

2026-03-13 14:05 - Action items assigned (Miguel Santos): 1) Prepare final credit recommendation (Aisha) 2) Extend aggregation job tests and add e2e dedupe verification (Rajiv) 3) Audit last 180 days for similar duplicates (Data Eng) 4) Add alerting for aggregate_per_day growth > 2x baseline (SRE).

2026-03-14 11:30 - Follow-up (Aisha Patel): Drafted credit calculation and preliminary postmortem. Recommending full refund of duplicated delta ($57.8k) and a goodwill credit of $5k, total $62.8k. Sending to Finance for approval.
resolution: hotfix deployed to prevent duplicate writes; backfill run; credit recommendation pending Finance approval
next_steps: 1) Finance to approve credit and issue to Atlas (due 2026-03-16). 2) Add e2e integration test for aggregation dedupe (owner: Rajiv, estimate 5). 3) Add Grafana alert and automated scan job for duplicate aggregates (owner: SRE, estimate 3). 4) Postmortem doc to be published to Confluence and linked to ticket.
